content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Health Checks and Restart Policies in Docker"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensuring high availability for containerized applications requires robust monitoring and automated recovery mechanisms. Docker provides built-in tools for this through Health Checks and Restart Policies."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Docker Restart Policies"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Restart policies dictate how Docker should handle containers when they exit. This is critical for maintaining uptime without relying entirely on external orchestrators."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"no: Do not automatically restart the container (default)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"always: Always restart the container if it stops, regardless of the exit status."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"on-failure: Restart the container only if it exits with a non-zero exit status."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"unless-stopped: Always restart the container unless it was explicitly stopped by the user."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Restart Policies via CLI"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can apply a restart policy directly when running a new container using the --restart flag."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"docker run -d --restart unless-stopped --name my_web_app nginx"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Health Checks"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"While restart policies monitor if a process exits, Health Checks determine if the application inside the container is actually functioning properly, even if the process is still running."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --retries=3 CMD curl -f http://localhost/ || exit 1"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Health Check Parameters Explained"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--interval: The time between health checks (e.g., 30 seconds)."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--timeout: Maximum time allowed for one check to complete before it is considered failed."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--retries: Consecutive failures required to transition the container status to unhealthy."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Combining Health Checks with Restart Policies"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, restart policies do not look at health check statuses. However, you can use external tools or write scripts to leverage container health states for automated orchestration and recovery."}]
